subject: Post-demo: model shortlist snapshot + benchmark links
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pratt <jpratt@aurelia.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist snapshot + benchmark links

Jordan — thanks again for the demo session today. Quick recap and the shortlist we discussed so your team can start internal alignment. I kept this intentionally focused so you can forward to procurement/engineering.

Summary of needs we captured during the call:
- Real-time chat with 200ms p99 target for 2k concurrent users (expected 10 req/s steady per shard)
- Named-entity extraction + short-form summarization quality target: >92% on internal eval set
- Data residency: US-only; logs retained for 30 days (customer requested)

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs and rationale):
1) Redwood-RT-7B (quantized 4-bit) — Cost-optimized, typical p50 ~80ms, p95 ~250ms; excellent token cost (approx $0.8 / 1M tokens in our hosted pricing). Good fit if you want to lower unit economics and can tolerate occasional quality delta on long tails.
2) Redwood-BAL-13B — Balanced quality/latency. p50 ~120ms, p95 ~320ms; best fit for your NER + summarization targets with modest compute. Higher cost (~$2.8 / 1M tokens) but reduces regression risk.
3) OpenHawk-70B (float16) — Highest quality; p50 ~260ms, p95 ~600ms; recommended for tiered flows (high-value cases where accuracy matters). Significant cost and requires Dedicated capacity for consistent latency.

Benchmarks and artifacts attached / linked:
- aurelia_postdemo_benchmarks.csv (attached): per-model latency percentiles, throughput under simulated load, token costs
- prompt_set_aurelia_v1.txt (attached): the prompt/response seed set we used for the quality runs
- Live benchmark page: https://redwood.prod/docs/benchmarks/aurelia-aug2027
- Eval folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-aurelia-evals

Quality/regression notes:
- The BAL-13B configuration includes a tuned prompt template that reduces hallucination on your summary use-case; attach includes a short examples file.
- For RT-7B we observed a 2.4% drop on the long-tail entity recall compared to BAL-13B; we can run a targeted fine-tuning/eval pass if you want to prioritize cost-oriented deployment.

Next suggested steps:
- If procurement wants pricing & commitment options, I can generate a Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison for a 3-month pilot. (Karthik will scope the Dedicated numbers.)
- Vanessa to propose a canary rollout plan (recommended: 2-week canary, 0.5% of traffic -> 5% -> 25%).
- Jordan — would you like the prompt set expanded to include your internal examples? If so, please share 50 representative pairs and we’ll run a targeted regression check.

Attachments: aurelia_postdemo_benchmarks.csv (csv, 120KB); prompt_set_aurelia_v1.txt (txt, 8KB); cost-latency-matrix.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min follow-up tomorrow if useful.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jordan Pratt <jpratt@aurelia.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurelia Procurement <procure@aurelia.io>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist snapshot + benchmark links

Thanks Marissa — very clear, appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifying points before we loop in procurement: 

1) For the BAL-13B runs, can you share the exact eval metric breakdown (precision/recall/F1) for the NER seed set? The CSV has aggregated scores but procurement wants the breakdown.
2) On regressions: that 2.4% delta on RT-7B — is that based on zero-shot prompts or with the prompt template applied? Any chance you can run a single-shot pass with two in-context examples from our set?
3) Regarding Dedicated — our infra team flagged the SLA for p95. If we go Dedicated, what guarantees can we reasonably expect for p95 under sustained 2k concurrent users?

If possible, can you get those answers by EOD tomorrow? Procurement wants a draft commercial email to review on Wednesday.

—Jordan
Jordan Pratt | Head of Product Engineering, Aurelia
jpratt@aurelia.io | +1 (650) 555-2634

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pratt <jpratt@aurelia.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist snapshot + benchmark links

Jordan — answers inline and concrete next steps below.

1) BAL-13B metric breakdown: attached CSV now includes the per-class precision / recall / F1 for the NER seed set (column headers: entity_type, precision, recall, f1). Quick highlights: overall F1 0.925; person/org recall ~0.94; product/location recall ~0.90. I also uploaded a short summary to the drive (see links).

2) RT-7B regression context: the 2.4% recall delta was measured with the RT-7B prompt template (the same template in prompt_set_aurelia_v1.txt). We can run a 1-shot and 2-shot pass with two of your representative pairs — happy to queue that today. Expect results in ~6 hours once we have the examples. If you share the five highest-priority pairs, we’ll run the quick checks and include token-level diffs.

3) Dedicated SLA for p95: with a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 2k concurrent users (we estimate 3x the base shard size for buffer), we can commit to a 99.5% availability SLA and best-effort p95 latency targets; for contractual p95 SLOs we typically negotiate explicit capacity buffer + burst policies. Karthik will provide the precise capacity/price math in the pilot quote.

Proposed immediate plan (week 0 pilot):
- Today: Jordan shares up to 5 representative prompt/response pairs (anonymized). Redwood runs 1-shot/2-shot checks on RT-7B and BAL-13B and returns token-level diffs (ETA today).
- Wed: Redwood sends a Hosted vs Dedicated 30-day pilot pricing comparison + canary rollout playbook (Vanessa).
- Thu: Procurement review — Marissa to supply draft commercial email + standard terms; Aurelia to confirm PO path.

If that timeline works, I’ll open a HubSpot task and link the DocuSign pricing draft once Karthik and I finalize numbers.
